subject: Follow-up: hosting boundaries and fallback options for TriadBank pilot
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: TriadBank pilot — call recap and suggested pilot plan

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything on one thread. 

Call highlights:
- TriadBank needs production data to remain within EU boundaries (accounting/legal requirement).
- Pilot scope: validation of core inference flows for transaction scoring (non-PII subset) + logging/trace requirements.
- Long-term options under consideration: Redwood Hosted (EU region), Redwood Dedicated (EU GPUs, reserved capacity), Private VPC / on-prem for parts of the workload that must not leave bank-controlled networks.
- APAC staff access: staff in APAC will need low-latency access for read-only analytics; Triad asked about safe cross-region routing or read-only replication.

Proposed pilot approach (recommended):
1) Week 0–4: Hosted (EU) pilot using our EU region with strict tenant isolation and prefix caching. This lets you validate functionality quickly.
2) Parallel: collect exact list of datasets and data-classification levels that are not allowed to leave bank premises. If any datasets require air-gapped processing, those will be scoped for Private or on-prem components.
3) Post-pilot: decide between moving to Dedicated EU (fast path, SLA + reserved throughput) or Private VPC/on-prem for restricted datasets. We can roadmap a hybrid (Hosted for front-end inference + Private for sensitive batch jobs).

Action items I propose:
- Sofia / procurement: confirm procurement timeline and whether the pilot can be run under a short MSAs or we need a formal SOW up front.
- Triad: send the data-classification matrix (high/medium/low) — I attached a template.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare a short SOW for a 4-week Hosted EU pilot and include an optional Dedicated transition estimate.
- Redwood (Ben): provide SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM options, and network connectivity checklist.

Attachments: triad-pilot-mpa-draft.pdf (draft MPA for pilot), data-classification-matrix.xlsx (template)

If that plan looks sensible I can lock in calendar times for an engineering sync next week (Marissa and Ben to join).

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Zhang <p.zhang@triadbank.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TriadBank pilot — call recap and suggested pilot plan

Hi Dylan,

Appreciate the clear summary — this aligns with our internal takeaways. A couple of clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Data residency: production must remain in the EU for all transaction-level data. For the pilot we can put anonymized non-PII samples in the Hosted EU environment, but anything labeled High in our data-classification (account numbers, full transaction rows) cannot leave bank-controlled networks.

2) On-prem need: our payments reconciliation team requires an on-prem option for a small batch workflow. Can Redwood support a hybrid where inference for high-sensitivity jobs runs in a Private/on-prem runtime while lower-sensitivity scoring runs in hosted? What does that ops split look like?

3) KMS/HSM: we need encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys and a letter describing HSM options. Also SOC2 Type II report or summary is required for procurement.

4) APAC access: staff in Singapore need read access. We prefer read-only API routing with a regional proxy or caching to avoid cross-border data replication. Can you document recommended patterns and their compliance implications?

Procurement: I looped in Peter (procurement manager) — we expect a purchase order in ~6 weeks if the legal review goes smoothly.

Next steps for us: I will share the data-classification matrix and sample dataset list by Wed. If possible send the SOC2 summary and KMS note before then so procurement has materials to review.

Thanks,
Sofia Lopez
Head of Data Platform | TriadBank
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TriadBank pilot — call recap and suggested pilot plan

Sofia — thanks, that's helpful and clear. Below are direct answers and a short ops sketch.

On Tue, Jun 28, 2027 at 16:37 Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com> wrote:
> 1) Data residency: production must remain in the EU for all transaction-level data. For the pilot we can put anonymized non-PII samples in the Hosted EU environment, but anything labeled High in our data-classification cannot leave bank-controlled networks.

Answer: That matches our standard hybrid posture. For the pilot we can host in EU and restrict production dataset uploads to EU tenancy. For High datasets we would either: (a) run those jobs in a Private VPC connector where we do not persist customer prompts/outputs to our multi-tenant store or (b) use a Dedicated EU pool physically isolated to your tenancy with stricter audit/log retention controls. We'll outline both in the SOW.

> 2) On-prem need: can Redwood support a hybrid where inference for high-sensitivity jobs runs in Private/on-prem runtime while lower-sensitivity runs in hosted?

Answer: Yes — Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane that can deploy inference containers on-prem or into a customer VPC. In practice customers commonly run a small on-prem worker for the sensitive batch jobs and keep interactive low-latency calls on Hosted EU. We can sketch the network flows (attached KMS/HSM ops diagram will help).

> 3) KMS/HSM and SOC2

Answer: Ben will drop SOC2 summary and our KMS options in a separate email. High level: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS providers and can integrate with on-prem HSMs for Private deployments.

> 4) APAC access: staff in Singapore need read access; prefer read-only API routing with regional proxy or caching.

Answer: Two recommended patterns: (A) cross-region read-only proxy + cache in APAC that requests EU-hosted inference but only stores ephemeral, anonymized tokens; (B) replicate derived, non-sensitive embeddings to APAC read-only store. We will document compliance trade-offs; pattern (A) is usually simpler for audits as it avoids persistent cross-border copies.

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: prepare a 4-week Hosted EU pilot SOW with optional Dedicated transition and a short annex for Private/on-prem migration. Include a high-level ops diagram. (Due: Thu EOB)
- Ben: send SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM note — include procedure for customer-managed keys and HSM key wrapping. (Due: Wed)
- Dylan: assemble recommended cross-region read-only patterns and a compliance summary for procurement.

Sofia, once we have the SOW and SOC2/KMS note I will set up a procurement/technical sync with Peter + your engineering lead.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
